career_stops.line: Entry job, treated it like a coordinator audition. Noted.
First real playbook. Left the offense better than they found it.
Took the big job young. The film is chaotic and occasionally brilliant.

buyout.descriptor: They would grumble, then pay it before lunch.

why_this_coach: The film shows a builder who gets bored the moment the thing works. Every stop got a new scheme, every exit came a season earlier than expected, and the results traveled anyway. That is not a flaw in the comp. That is the comp.
screenshot_line: YOU ARE THE COORDINATOR WHO TOOK THE BIG JOB EARLY AND MADE THE CHAOS LOOK LIKE A PLAN.
scouting_report: Candidate profiles as a scheme-first operator with a fast internal clock. The resume reads like a coordinator tree: each stop shorter than the last, each exit with the numbers pointing up. The committee does not view the movement as instability — the movement IS the development plan.

In the room, the candidate answers the temperament questions like a play-caller: aggressive on fourth down, keeps score quietly, and admits the staff does more of the work than the legend suggests. That self-awareness is rarer than the talent.
Long-term projection: give this one a program with a low ceiling and watch the ceiling move. Just do not ask for a ten-year commitment in the introductory presser.
best_fit_program: A proud program two bad seasons removed from relevance, with an administration that answers texts after midnight.

runner_ups.note: If the weird ideas ever fully take the wheel.
The floor outcome if the itch wins every time.
